title: Gullak Season 5 Returns June 5. If You're an NRI Who Hasn't Watched This Show, You've Been Homesick for No Reason.
excerpt: The Mishra family is back on SonyLIV with new cast members, a house renovation, and the same quietly devastating emotional punches that made four seasons of this show the best-kept secret in Indian streaming.
body:
There is a very specific kind of loneliness that comes from living 8,000 miles away from a family you love but can't visit often enough. It lives in the silence between weekly video calls, in the way your mother's kitchen looks slightly different every time you FaceTime, in the realization that your nephew has grown a foot since you last saw him. For the last five years, Gullak has been the antidote to that loneliness.

Season 5 arrives on SonyLIV on June 5, 2026, and the trailer confirms both good news and change.

## The Mishras Are Renovating. Everything Else Is the Same.

The new season finds Santosh Mishra and his family renovating their modest home — a plotline that will resonate with anyone whose parents have spent twenty years talking about redoing the kitchen and then finally, inexplicably, started during the hottest month of the year. Annu is still navigating adulthood. Santosh is still navigating his wife's expectations. And Shanti Mishra — played with devastating precision by Geetanjali Kulkarni — is still the emotional center of gravity around which every story in this universe orbits.

The biggest change: Vaibhav Raj Gupta, who played the older son Anand for four seasons, has been replaced by Anant Joshi. The show has addressed this quietly, without fanfare, which is very Gullak. In a streaming landscape where recasts become three-day Twitter controversies, the Gullak team seems to have trusted its audience to accept the change and move on. Whether that trust was earned will be clear by episode two.

## Why NRIs Watch This Show Differently

Gullak is not a show about nostalgia. It's a show about a family that is so ordinary, so precisely rendered, that it becomes extraordinary.

Every diaspora viewer has their own version of the Mishras. The father who will not spend money on himself but will silently transfer it when his kid is in trouble. The mother who communicates love through irritation. The brother who left for a better city and feels guilty about it, but not guilty enough to come back.

When Gullak debuted in 2019, it was an afterthought on a platform that barely registered in the streaming wars. By season three, word of mouth — particularly in NRI WhatsApp groups and Indian student communities abroad — had turned it into one of SonyLIV's most-watched Hindi originals. By season four, it had won a Filmfare OTT Award and had been recommended by everyone from film critics to homesick software engineers in New Jersey.

The show's power lies in its refusal to be dramatic. There are no villains. No affairs. No sudden deaths designed to spike engagement. The conflict in a typical Gullak episode is whether the family can afford a new cooler, or whether the younger son should take a job he doesn't want. These are not small stakes. They're the stakes that define most Indian middle-class lives — and most of the phone calls NRIs make on Sunday mornings.

## The Streaming Landscape Has Changed. Gullak Hasn't.

Since season four premiered in 2024, Indian OTT has undergone a dramatic shift. JioHotstar consolidated its grip. Netflix India went all-in on thrillers and crime. Prime Video banked on big-name talent. The shows that get the most attention are the loudest ones — spy franchises, true-crime adaptations, celebrity-driven limited series.

Gullak has never competed in that arena. It doesn't need to. It operates in the emotional register of a handwritten letter in an era of push notifications. It's the show you watch when the algorithm has exhausted every other option and you just want to feel something real.

The five-episode format means you can watch the entire season in a single evening, which is both a gift and a complaint. By the time you've finished, you'll want more. That's been true every season.

## What to Expect

Based on the trailer: the house renovation will serve as the season's spine, with each family member's relationship to the changing home reflecting their own evolution. There are hints of Annu's romantic life becoming more central, and Santosh's quiet crisis about whether a renovated house will still feel like his house.

The new Anand will need to earn his place quickly. Vaibhav Raj Gupta's understated performance was one of the show's cornerstones, and replacing him without explanation will test even the most loyal viewer.

But if four seasons have taught us anything, it's that the Gullak team knows what it's doing. They've never chased trends. They've never raised their voice. They've just kept telling the story of one family, one small moment at a time, and trusting that the audience would find them.

For NRIs, that audience has always been there. It just took a few thousand miles of distance to realize how much this show was about them.

*Gullak Season 5 streams on SonyLIV from June 5, 2026. All five episodes drop the same day.*
author: Diaspora Desk
